summary.goal:
Extend this tiny todo library. Add to src/todo.js:
- toggle(id): flips the item's done flag and returns the item; throws an Error whose message contains "Unknown id" for an unknown id.
- remove(id): deletes the item and returns true, or returns false when the id is unknown.
- count(): returns the number of items.
Keep add(text) and list() working as they are (list returns a copy). Add tests for the new methods in test/ using node:test, and write a README.md that documents createStore, add, list, toggle, remove and count with a short example. npm test must stay green.

tasks.title: Implement toggle, remove and count in src/todo.js
tasks.spec:
Extend the object returned by createStore() in src/todo.js with three new methods, keeping add and list unchanged in behavior (list still returns a shallow copy).

Contract (an item is { id, text, done }):
- toggle(id): find the item whose id === id, flip its done flag, return the stored item object. If no item matches, throw new Error('Unknown id: ' + id) so the message contains the substring "Unknown id".
- remove(id): find and remove the item; return true. If no item matches, return false (must not throw).
- count(): return the current number of items.

Required internal change: add currently sets id from items.length + 1. After a removal that would reuse an id still held by a surviving item, so replace it with an internal monotonically increasing counter (e.g. nextId starting at 1, incremented on each add) so ids remain unique and are never reused.

Keep the existing concise single-line method style, ESM named export, 2-space indent; do not add dependencies, classes or new files. Verify with `npm test` (the existing test must still pass).

acceptance.review: Confirm toggle flips and returns the live stored item, unknown toggle throws an Error whose message contains "Unknown id", remove returns true/false correctly, count tracks adds and removes, list still returns a new array, and ids stay unique after a removal (add, remove, add does not duplicate an id).

report.summary: Extended createStore() in src/todo.js with toggle, remove and count, and replaced length-based id generation with a monotonic nextId counter so ids stay unique after removals. add and list are unchanged (list still returns items.slice()).
report.evidence: `npm test` exited 0 (existing "add and list" test passes, 1/1). An inline node:assert/strict script also exited 0, confirming: count() 0 then 2; add ids 1 and 2; toggle(1) returns the same stored object and flips done true then false; toggle(99) throws an Error with message containing "Unknown id"; remove(1) returns true then false; after removal the next add returns id 3, and list() ids are unique [2,3]; pushing onto list()'s result does not change count().
decisions: Used `let nextId = 1` with `id: nextId++` in add, per the design's suggested counter approach, to guarantee ids are never reused after a removal.
remove uses findIndex + splice; toggle uses find and mutates the stored item, matching the 'return the live object' contract.
Kept the existing compact single-line method style and 2-space indentation; no classes, helpers, deps or new files.
openIssues: Tests for the new methods and README.md are separate tasks and outside this task's file scope (src/todo.js), so they were not written here.

tasks.title: Add node:test coverage for toggle, remove and count
tasks.spec:
Add tests for the new store methods under test/, using node:test and node:assert/strict, following the existing style in test/todo.test.js (import test from 'node:test'; import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; a fresh createStore() per test). You may extend test/todo.test.js or add a new file matching test/*.test.js; keep the existing 'add and list' test passing.

Cover at least:
- toggle flips done from false to true and back on a second call, and returns the affected item (assert the returned object's done value and that it is reflected in list()).
- toggle on an unknown id throws, asserted via assert.throws with a /Unknown id/ matcher.
- remove returns true and the item disappears (count and list reflect it); remove on an unknown id returns false and does not throw.
- count returns 0 for a fresh store and tracks adds and removes.
- list returns a copy: mutating the returned array does not change the store (e.g. push then count unchanged).
- ids are not reused after a removal: add two items, remove the first, add another, and assert the new item's id differs from the removed one and from the surviving one.

Verify with `npm test`.

acceptance.review: Confirm the tests exercise the specified edge cases (unknown-id throw with the "Unknown id" message, remove returning false, count after add/remove, list copy semantics, id uniqueness after removal) and that they would fail against a store missing these methods.

report.summary: Extended test/todo.test.js with node:test coverage for toggle, remove and count, keeping the existing 'add and list' test. Seven new tests cover: toggle flipping done false->true->false and returning the live item (asserted identical to the object add returned and reflected via list()), toggle on an unknown id throwing /Unknown id/, remove returning true and shrinking list/count, remove on unknown id returning false without throwing, count from 0 tracking adds and removes, list returning a copy (push on the returned array leaves count unchanged), and id uniqueness after a removal (new id differs from both the removed and surviving ids). Style matches the existing file: ESM default import of node:test, assert/strict, a fresh createStore() per test, 2-space indentation.
report.evidence: Ran `npm test` from the project root: exit code 0, 8 tests, 8 pass, 0 fail (log shows all seven new test names passing alongside the original 'add and list'). The tests reference s.toggle, s.remove and s.count, so they would error against a store lacking those methods; the unknown-id assertions use assert.throws(fn, /Unknown id/) which requires the exact 'Unknown id' message.
decisions: Extended the existing test/todo.test.js rather than adding a new file, to keep the project's single test file and existing style; this is within scope (test/**) and package.json's test glob picks it up unchanged.

tasks.title: Write README.md documenting the store API
tasks.spec: Create README.md at the project root documenting the tiny todo library. It must mention and explain createStore along with add, list, toggle, remove and count: what each returns, that list returns a copy, that toggle throws for an unknown id, and that remove returns false for an unknown id. Include a short, accurate runnable example in a fenced js code block that imports { createStore } from './src/todo.js' and demonstrates add, list, toggle, remove and count. Keep it concise; no API behavior beyond what src/todo.js implements.

acceptance.review: Confirm every documented method matches the implemented contract (return values, list copy, toggle throwing for unknown ids, remove returning false for unknown ids) and that the example is accurate.

report.summary: Created README.md at the project root documenting the whole public API of the tiny todo library: createStore() plus add, list, toggle, remove and count. Each method entry states its return value and the edge-case behavior from the implemented contract — list returns a new shallow copy each call (elements are the live item objects), toggle throws an Error whose message contains "Unknown id" for an unknown id, remove returns false (and does not throw) for an unknown id, count returns the current item count. The README also notes that ids are unique and never reused after a removal, and includes a short fenced js example that imports { createStore } from './src/todo.js' and demonstrates add, list, toggle (including the thrown error), remove and count. No API behavior beyond what src/todo.js implements is documented.
report.evidence: `npm test` from the project root: 8 tests, 8 pass, 0 fail (exit 0). Acceptance greps: all six of createStore, add, list, toggle, remove, count found in README.md. Accuracy of the example was verified by extracting the fenced js block from README.md verbatim, rewriting only the import path to an absolute path (so it could run from /tmp without writing files into the shared project tree) and running it with node: output was `2 / 2 / true / Unknown id: 999 / true / false / 1`, matching every inline comment in the example exactly. `git status --short` shows only README.md as new; src/todo.js and test/todo.test.js remain the other executors' modifications, untouched by me.
decisions: Documented each method as a bullet under a single Usage section rather than one heading per method, to keep the README concise as the task asked.
Included a short Tests section noting that `npm test` runs the suite, since the README is the only user-facing doc and the script is the project's stated verification command.
